A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, references, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original Cora experiments comparing graph-network architectures and weight rescaling in Figures 1 and 8, plus grid-graph sensitivity experiments in Appendix B, Figure 7.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results: Cora experiments in Figures 1 and 8 and grid-graph sensitivity experiments in Appendix C, Figure 7.

M1.justification: The architectures and message-passing variants remain unchanged. The computational-bottleneck definition foregrounded in v3 was already present in v1's appendix; this is not a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Cora and the 10-by-10 grid and retain the same illustrative graph scenarios. The two-radius and ring-transfer tasks mentioned in v3 Appendix E belong to discussed prior work, not new evaluations.

E2.justification: Figures 1 and 8 retain GCN, GAT, SAGE, and GIN; Figure 7 retains GCN with different embedding sizes. Newly cited methods are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported RQ specification changes: v1 Appendix A.2, Equation 6 uses the normalized Laplacian, whereas v3 Section 2.1 and Appendix B.2 define RQ using the combinatorial Laplacian and separately describe its normalized variant. This revises the stated metric specification without establishing that experiments were rerun. Other experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The same weight-rescaling, architecture, metric, and depth comparisons are retained, alongside the grid sensitivity analysis across embedding sizes. Appendix E adds discussion rather than new ablations, robustness tests, or case-study results.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 random seeds for the Cora experiments and retain identical shaded plots. No repeated-run information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is added or changed.

E6.justification: Figures 1, 7, and 8 retain identical empirical plots and findings, including architecture-dependent smoothing behavior and delayed sensitivity collapse with larger embeddings. No original result entries or numerical findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 corrects the normalized Laplacian's degree factors from D^(1/2) to D^(-1/2), adds validity conditions and spectral properties, and distinguishes RQ variants. Definition 4.1 and its multiset construction already appeared in v1 Appendix A.4; their promotion does not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The nine challenged beliefs and the central claims about separability, task dependence, and distinct computational/topological bottlenecks remain. The revised abstract explicitly frames counterexamples as refuting universal statements, without materially changing the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix E explains that the proposed conceptual separation is pedagogical rather than a practical diagnostic method and discusses complementary capacity, sensitivity, and vanishing-gradient perspectives. Section 3.2 also qualifies the DGN-versus-MLP argument by separating it from denoising and regularization benefits.

D1.justification: v3 adds an experimental-code repository pointer in the introduction. Section 2.1 now states that the experiment follows Roth and Liebig's procedure, replacing the looser description of being inspired by it. These improve documentation without demonstrating an implementation change.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused citations and an alternative-views discussion engaging Blayney et al., Mishayev et al., and Kormann et al. It explains how their practical or empirical perspectives relate to this paper's conceptual aim, while retaining the existing research framework.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected passages are edited, section summaries become calls to action, and existing definitions are brought into the main text. Appendices are reorganized and an alternative-views appendix is added, but most prose and the main argumentative sequence remain.

P2.justification: The original belief-and-reference table becomes a compact main-text table plus an appendix reference table. Figure 3 adopts labels already present in v1 Figure 6. Conference styling, summary-box appearance, captions, and figure placement change, while empirical graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision and accessibility by correcting degree normalization, foregrounding an existing key definition, adding a code-access pointer, and explaining its scope relative to alternative views. These are useful refinements to the same scientific argument and evidence. The improvement is limited by remaining metric ambiguity: Appendix B.2 reverses the normalized and unnormalized Laplacian terminology in one explanatory sentence.
